## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `88a02ae6a6386e9f121874bc0f7fc8f2ada1bd58`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-11-16T05:17Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6907857563; hand-off 6907745553 and lane request 6907758207 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Reviewed: the whole diff, `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` (+386/−3), every hunk. Read to judge it and not reviewed: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` (`markerMatches`, `latestMarkedComment`, `OS_DEV_REPORT_MARKER`, `devReportPayloadCandidates`), `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` (`recordAuthorTrusted`, `recordTrustedAuthors`), `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` (`deliveredCardNumber`), `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, and the pm-dispatch references `l1-review-checklist.md`, `landing-operations.md`, `contract-review.md`. `record-recognisers --template` on main reads this file list as the declaration face, so the header carries no `Scope:` and no `Security-touching:` line; ④ is added because the hand-off asked for a full read of a landing gate.

### ① Derived judgments

**Card acceptance.**

- Ask 1 (marked pull lands only on a report whose `dogfood_battery` names the head, or an ancestor differing by merges of main): met. `landDogfoodGate` runs in `foldStroke` before the comment file is read, so a refusal is exit 2 with nothing packed or sent. The head match is a prefix test on a 7 to 40 hex sha; the ancestor walk is first-parent, each step a two-parent commit whose second parent the base holds. I checked the compare direction: `compare/P2...BASE` answering `ahead` or `identical` does mean P2 is an ancestor of the base tip. `--land` cannot reach the two landing ops without `--comment-file` (`parseOptions`, pinned by an existing case), so there is no second path through this file.
- Ask 2 (the refusal names the title, the report comment id and the battery text): met for the comment id and the text; the title itself is not printed. See S1.
- Ask 3 (three self-test rows): met. `!` with `n/a` refused, `!` with a run on the head passes, no marker is not judged with the same four reads as before. The battery adds both directions for the merge walk, the hop cap at and one past, the page cap, newest-report ordering both ways, and one case per refusal reason keyed on that reason's own text. The self-test is a CI gate (`check:pm-label-write` in `lint.yml`) and the count is pinned (37, floor 17).
- The card's ⛔ holds: no workflow file and no dogfood shard on `pull_request` is touched.

**Which pulls are classified, against the rest of the tooling.**

- The two markers are exactly the rule's: `os-dev.md:273` says title `!`, or a `(narrowing)` arm on the `Clause-②:` line, either value. `l1-review-checklist.md:48` and `contract-review.md:10` say the same. The card's own sentence can be read as a title spelling of the arm; no rule text and no reader in the tree knows such a spelling, so reading the arm off the body line through `readClause2Line` is the correct reading of the card, not a deviation from it.
- The body line is read first-declaration-wins, the same way `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads the same body (`declarationFromPullRequest`), so the landing gate and the Check Changeset job cannot disagree about one body's arm.
- A `malformed` line refuses. A near-miss line and an absent line are both read as no arm. See S2.
- The changeset's own breaking signals (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` `breakingDeclaration`: the banner, a `major`, a bang summary, the arm on the changeset body) are not read. The rule the card enforces does not name them either, so this is an observation, not a finding. See N1.

**What counts as a battery on the head.**

- The newest `os-dev-report` on the delivered card, among rows by the relay identity or a governed approver. The marker is anchored at the body start, so a comment that quotes the marker is not a report; newest-of is `latestMarkedComment` (created_at, thread order on a tie). The payload is read with the patrol's candidates. No second parser, and the structural case pins that.
- `n/a` and a text naming no sha both refuse, so both measured texts from the card (`n/a: no ! in the PR title…` and `not run: the title carries no breaking marker`) are refused on a `!` title.
- The gate judges the sha only. A text that opens with the head sha and then reports failures passes; `l1-review-checklist.md:48` still owns "full, and red fixed or reported" at ACCEPT. This matches the card's ask 1 and I do not ask for more. See N2.

**Misfire on a pull that needs none.** An unmarked pull returns before any new read; pinned by the read list. One new refusal reaches unmarked pulls: a title that does not read on step ①, which the issues endpoint always answers for a real pull. A marked pull with no card, or whose report sits on another thread, refuses with the remedy printed; that is the fail-closed direction and the rule owes such a pull a battery in every case.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — Card ask 2 says the refusal names the title. The line prints the marker as the words "`!` before the colon of the title" and never the title text, while the narrowing marker does quote its line. The measured defect was a report line contradicting the title; printing both side by side is the point of ask 2. Quote the title (capped, as `quoteLine` does) in `landDogfoodRefusal` and assert it in the case that already checks the other four fields.
- S2 (should-fix) — The header says an unreadable marker fails closed, and `landDogfoodMarkers` refuses a `malformed` line for that reason. A line that `readClause2Line` answers as a near miss is treated as no arm and the pull is not judged, and no case pins that reading either way. `clause2-line.mjs` states that collapsing its readings into "no" is the defect it was written against. Either refuse a near miss, or keep it not judged, say so in the header beside the `malformed` rule, and pin it with a case. I accept either; an absent line staying not judged is right and agrees with Check Changeset.
- S3 (should-fix) — Nothing in the pm-dispatch skill says `--land` now judges this. `landing-operations.md:60` still reads as "green, then one relay stroke", and no ↔ case binds the rule text to the gate the way the existing fold case binds `--land` to that file. The tool's refusal line and `--help` do teach the remedy, and `l1-review-checklist.md:48` already gives the seat the rule, so nothing contradicts. A clause on line 60 in place (no added line) plus one ↔ case closes it; that edit touches governed rules text, so a follow-up card is an acceptable way to pay it. Say which in the next report.
- N1 (nit) — `titleBreakingMarker` cuts at the first colon of the title; the changeset-side reader anchors on type, optional scope, `!:`. The two agree on all 29 bang subjects in main's history. A header sentence naming the title form the gate reads would keep the two from drifting.
- N2 (nit) — The ✓ line prints the battery text but not that only its sha was judged. Three words ("sha judged only") would stop a reader taking ✓ for the checklist's line 48.
- N3 (nit) — A rate-limited or failed gate read is reported as a REFUSAL at exit 2, where every other unread in this file is exit 3 (prerequisite). The stroke writes nothing either way.
- N4 (nit) — With several pulls delivering one card (`Part of`), the newest report may belong to a sibling pull, and the marked pull is refused until its own report is newest again. Fail-closed and the remedy is printed; the report's `pr` field could pick the right row.
- N5 (nit) — The truncation refusal's remedy says to land by hand. `landing-operations.md` sends every landing through this stroke; word the remedy as "report to the maintainer" or name the documented route.

No must-fix.

### ② Semver level

`scripts/pm/**` only; nothing published, no package touched, no changeset owed (`skip-changeset` label; Check Changeset is green). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body are true for this diff. The PR title carries no `!` and the body no arm, so the report's `dogfood_battery: n/a` is correct for this pull by the gate's own rule.

CI on this head: 48 check-runs; 24 success, 23 skipped, 1 still in progress (Test Core 1/8). Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Dogfood Regression Gate are success. ⛔ This PASS is rendered while one check is running: the seat waits for Test Core 1/8 to read success before it lands, and a red there is not covered by this record.
CI completed before posting: 49 check-runs on this head, 26 success, 23 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (ignore reports by untrusted authors): keep, option A. It is the record leg's own author set, read through the same two functions, and a landing gate must not be opened by text any commenter can post.
- Open question 2 (the arm read from the body's `Clause-②:` line, not the title): option A, for the reasons under ①.
- Deviation, readers imported from their owners: confirmed, and it is the better shape. Each imported module guards its CLI behind `isEntrypoint`; `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` was already in this file's load closure through `check-half-states.mjs`; none of them imports `label-write.mjs` back. The tooling self-tests job is green on this head, which is the load proof.
- Deviation, attribution lines above `Fixes #34204`: `deliveredCardNumber` reads the closing keyword anywhere in the body; PR-body guards is green.
- `security_findings: none` from the dev: I add nothing to the public record under this heading. The residual risks of a point-in-time landing gate are noted to the seat privately.
- SQL push-down check: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The gate holds against the scenario it was accepted for. Both measured roots (#32926, #33431) carried `!` in the title with a report saying the battery was not applicable or not run; both texts are refused here before `pr_ready`, with the report comment and its text on the line. The placement is right: before the comment is judged, on the read step ① already makes, so an unmarked pull pays nothing. The walk is the narrowest test that still lets a seat merge main after the battery, and it refuses every shape it cannot prove (one parent, three parents, a second parent off the base, an unread commit or compare, the cap). The reuse of the patrol's and the record leg's readers means the gate cannot grow a private dialect of "report", "newest" or "trusted".

What it is not: it is a check at the moment of the stroke on text the dev wrote, not a proof that the battery ran or was green, and not a replacement for the L1 line. The header says as much ("NOT MEASURED is never a pass") and S3 asks the skill to say where the gate sits.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `524fac67e4d4c1d39e9914ed939c835df501804d`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-11-16T06:08Z. Delta review of this head against PASS 6908045917 at 88a02ae6; claim: comment 6908763313; hand-off 6908721317 and lane request 6908734327 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Reviewed: the net diff of this head against main, `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` (+456/−3), and inside it every hunk of the round (`88a02ae6..01ad0b0e1`, +114/−44, two commits: `468c5ac4d` the fixes, `01ad0b0e1` one added case). Read to judge it and not reviewed: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (`quoteLine`, `readClause2Line` and its three near-miss reasons), `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (`declarationFromPullRequest`), `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, `landing-operations.md`. `record-recognisers --template` reads this file list as the declaration face, and main's rules print no `Scope:` and no `Security-touching:` line on that face, so the header carries neither; ④ is kept because the prior record carried it for a landing gate.

### ① Derived judgments

**What moved between the two heads.**

- The PR's own commits: `468c5ac4d` and `01ad0b0e1`, both `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs` only.
- The main merge `524fac67e` (second parent `22bcc7699`, 13 commits of main): `git show --remerge-diff` prints no hunk, so the merge resolved nothing by hand and adds no content of its own. Main did not touch `label-write.mjs`. It did move two modules the gate imports from; the five imported readers (`markerMatches`, `latestMarkedComment`, `devReportPayloadCandidates`, `OS_DEV_REPORT_MARKER`, `deliveredCardNumber`) are byte-identical on both sides of the merge, so the gate reads through the same code the prior record judged. The diff against main is still one file.

**Prior findings.**

- S1 (title not quoted): closed. `landDogfoodGate` carries `title` on every judged result, quoted through `quoteLine` at `LAND_TITLE_QUOTE_CAP` (160), and `landDogfoodRefusal` prints it first, JSON-quoted. The four-field case now asserts `title: "fix(pm)!: a breaking fixture"` beside the marker, comment id, battery text, reason and remedy; a second case pins the cap and its ellipsis both ways.
- S2 (near-miss line read as no arm): closed, by the first of the two routes I offered. `landDogfoodMarkers` refuses `near-miss` on the same branch as `malformed`, names the reason, and the remedy now says which line to fix (`clear` travels with the reading instead of one shared sentence). The header and the jsdoc say so beside the `malformed` rule; an absent line stays not judged and says "as Check Changeset reads it". Pinned at the marker function and through the whole stroke, both for the near miss (exit 2, zero sends) and for the absent line (exit 0, "not judged"). See N2 for which reason the pin exercises.
- S3 (the skill does not say `--land` judges this): open, on the route the prior record allowed. No rules text is in this PR; the body now opens `Part of #34204` and names the clause on `landing-operations.md:60` plus its ↔ case as remainder 2, so landing this pull does not close the card. #34301, which the dev was waiting on for that file, is in this head's main merge, so nothing blocks the remainder now. Carried below as S1.
- N1 (title form not named): closed. The header and `titleBreakingMarker`'s jsdoc name the form read. The header also states a measurement (1331 bang subjects among 8521 on main at `22438726f`, none disagreeing with the changeset-side reader). I could not re-measure that figure: the review clone is shallow. On the 228 subjects it does hold, the two readers agree on all 30 bang subjects and disagree on none.
- N2 (✓ line silent on what was judged): closed. The line says "sha judged only", pinned in the passing case; the header adds that fullness and reds stay the L1 checklist's.
- N3 (an unanswered read reported as a refusal): closed. The four gate reads (pull, thread page, walk commit, compare) return `unread: true` when the call's verdict is not `ok`, and `foldStroke` exits 3 with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` and "NOTHING WAS WRITTEN" before the judged-refusal branch. Each is pinned at exit 3 with zero sends, a rate-limited read among them; every judged reason stays pinned at exit 2. The usage text names both exits. See N3 below for one read this classes loosely.
- N4 (a sibling pull's report shadows this pull's): closed. When the newest trusted report's `pr` names another pull, the gate takes the newest trusted report whose `pr` names this pull, or refuses naming the sibling's comment. Only a report naming another pull moves the gate: a newest report with a null `pr` still decides. Pinned three ways (sibling passed over, null stays newest, none naming this pull refuses) plus the reader's four readings. The selected report still has to name the head or a merge-of-base ancestor, so the fallback admits nothing the head test would not. See N1 below for the one ordering it leaves.
- N5 (truncation remedy said "by hand"): closed. The remedy is "report it to the maintainer", with the reason.

**Newly introduced, against the net diff.**

- A thread page that answers 200 with no list is now its own judged refusal (exit 2) instead of sharing the unread sentence. Correct split: the platform answered, the answer is unusable. Pinned (`01ad0b0e1`).
- `reportedPayloadString` generalises `reportedDogfoodBattery` over the key and is called for `pr` too; marker test and payload candidates are still the patrol's, so the "no second parser" property holds and the structural case still pins it.
- Reach of the S2 fix onto pulls that need no battery: an unmarked pull whose body carries a near-miss line and no declaration is now refused at `--land` until one line is written. That is the fail-closed direction I asked for and the remedy is one line; I checked it cannot fire when a real declaration is present, because `readClause2Line` returns the declaration first wherever the near miss sits.
- Battery count 37 to 46, floor unchanged; the count is pinned and the self-test is a CI gate.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix, continues S3) — The pm-dispatch skill still does not say `--land` judges a marked pull, and no ↔ case binds that text to the gate. Agreed route: remainder 2 on card #34204 after this pull lands. The card must stay open until it is paid; the seat confirms that at landing.
- N1 (nit, new, from the N4 fix) — When the newest report names a sibling pull, the fallback considers only reports whose `pr` names this pull, so a report for this pull written with a null `pr` is passed over there, although the same report decides when it is itself the newest. The header states the rule as written, so this is consistent; a case pinning that ordering, or a clause saying a null-`pr` report is not this pull's in the fallback, would make it deliberate.
- N2 (nit, new, from the S2 fix) — The near-miss refusal is pinned on the `spelling` reason only. `inline-key` is the reason real bodies are most likely to produce (this PR's own summary writes the key mid-sentence, and is saved only by its declaration line). One case on that reason would pin the branch where it will actually be met.
- N3 (nit, new, from the N3 fix) — A 404 on the card thread is classed as unread with the remedy "land again once the card reads". When the body names a card number that does not exist, that read never answers differently; the remedy could add "or correct the card the body names". Nothing is written either way.

No must-fix.

### ② Semver level

`scripts/pm/**` only; nothing published, no package touched, no changeset owed (`skip-changeset` label). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body are true for this diff. The title carries no `!` and the body no arm, so the report's `dogfood_battery: n/a` (os-dev-report 6908698877) is correct for this pull by the gate's own rule, and the gate would not judge this pull.

CI on this head: 48 check-runs, 26 success, 22 skipped, none failed, none running. Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Test UI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards and Dogfood Regression Gate are success. This PASS is not rendered ahead of any check.
CI completed before posting: 48 check-runs on this head, 26 success, 22 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, merge commit instead of rebase: confirmed harmless. The remerge diff is empty and the imported readers did not move; no force-push.
- Deviation, two ablations re-run with distinct replacements: a matter of the dev's evidence, not of the diff. I did not re-run them (`Local-runs: none`); the tooling self-tests job on this head is the proof I rely on.
- N4 was taken in this round although I graded it a nit. It adds one pure reader and one branch, is pinned both ways, and stays inside the one file; I accept it as in scope.
- `Fixes` became `Part of`: `deliveredCardNumber` reads both, and PR-body guards is green on this head.
- `security_findings: none` from the dev: I add nothing to the public record under this heading. The gate's fail-closed direction is unchanged by this round, and no new write path exists.
- SQL push-down check: the round adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The round makes the gate say more and assume less without moving what it accepts. The refusal now puts the title beside the report text, which is the side-by-side reading both measured roots (#32926, #33431) needed. The two exits now mean two different things, a verdict and a read that did not happen, which is how the rest of this file already speaks. The near-miss change closes the one place the marker read could answer "no" for a line it had not understood. The sibling-report rule narrows which report is read without loosening what that report must say. The limits stated in the prior record stand: this is a check at the moment of the stroke on text the dev wrote, not a proof that the battery ran or was green, and the L1 line keeps that duty; S1 is the sentence that tells the skill's reader so.

- 风险与回滚：只改 PM 工具一个文件；没标记的 PR 不判、照旧落地。回滚 = revert。
